chapterTitle: Chapter 3 Electronic Structure and Periodic Properties of Elements
title: 3. Check Your Learning

pages.text: Check Your Learning One of the frequencies used to transmit and receive cellular telephone signals in the United States is 850 MHz. What is the wavelength in meters of these radio waves?

Check Your Learning The microwaves in an oven are of a specific frequency that will heat the water molecules contained in food. (This is why most plastics and glass do not become hot in a microwave oven-they do not contain water molecules.) This frequency is about 3  109 Hz. What is the energy of one photon in these microwaves?
Check Your Learning Calculate the threshold energy in kJ/mol of electrons in aluminum, given that the lowest frequency photon for which the photoelectric effect is observed is 9.87  1014 Hz.
Check Your Learning The electron in Figure 3.15 is promoted even further to an orbit with n = 6. What is its new energy?
Check Your Learning What is the energy in joules and the wavelength in meters of the photon produced when an electron falls from the n = 5 to the n = 3 level in a He+ ion (Z = 2 for He+)?
Check Your Learning Calculate the wavelength of a softball with a mass of 100 g traveling at a velocity of 35 m s–1, assuming that it can be modeled as a single particle.
Check Your Learning Identify the subshell in which electrons with the following quantum numbers are found: (a) n = 3, l = 1; (b) n = 5, l = 3; (c) n = 2, l = 0.
Check Your Learning If a shell contains a maximum of 32 electrons, what is the principal quantum number, n?
Check Your Learning How many orbitals have l = 2 and n = 3?
Check Your Learning Identify the atoms from the electron configurations given: (a) [Ar]4s23d5 (b) [Kr]5s24d105p6
Check Your Learning Which ion with a +2 charge has the electron configuration 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p64d5? Which ion with a +3 charge has this configuration?
Check Your Learning Give an example of an atom whose size is smaller than fluorine.
Check Your Learning Which has the lowest value for IE1: O, Po, Pb, or Ba?
Check Your Learning Give the group name for each of the following elements: (a) krypton (b) selenium (c) barium (d) lithium
Check Your Learning Give the symbol and name for the ion with 34 protons and 36 electrons.
Check Your Learning Aluminum and carbon react to form an ionic compound. Predict which forms an anion, which forms a cation, and the charges of each ion. Write the symbol for each ion and name them.
Check Your Learning Predict the formula of the ionic compound formed between the sodium cation, Na+, and the sulfide anion, S2−.

Check Your Learning Predict the formula of the ionic compound formed between the lithium ion and the peroxide ion, (Hint: Use the periodic table to predict the sign and the charge on the lithium ion.)
Check Your Learning Using the periodic table, predict whether the following compounds are ionic or covalent: (a) SO2 (b) CaF2 (c) N2H4 (d) Al2(SO4)3
